topic: First human-to-human heart transplant: 3 December 1967, Groote Schuur Hospital, Cape Town, by Christiaan Barnard and a team of about 30; patient Louis Washkansky, 53, a grocer, lived 18 days (died of pneumonia). Donor Denise Darvall, 25, fatally injured by a car; her father Edward consented that night. Norman Shumway's Stanford team had developed the technique in dogs through the 1960s and performed the first US transplant on 6 January 1968. Second Cape Town patient Philip Blaiberg lived 19 months (593 days). ISHLT registry: median survival after adult heart transplant about 12–13 years.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: The first heart transplant was American — Stanford invented the operation.
myths.reality: Shumway's Stanford team developed the technique, but the first human transplant was Barnard's in Cape Town on 3 December 1967; Stanford's first followed on 6 January 1968.
